status: Computational scenarios; no biological experiment or independent peer review
reason: No fitted species-specific image/perception dataset; scenario ranges are not confidence bounds.

pecten-maximus.method: Select complementary central/peripheral sharpness masks on the same seabed photo. Mask radius and defocus are user assumptions, not a fitted scallop optical model.
pecten-maximus.evidence: A layered guanine mirror focuses light onto two retinal layers with different field coverage.
pecten-maximus.limits: No ray-traced eye, measured point-spread function, eye positions or neural fusion. The two panes are explanatory optical hypotheses, not two conscious views.
pecten-maximus.validation: Fit measured mirror geometry and retinal positions, then compare spatial predictions with independent behavior.
pecten-maximus.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

chironex-fleckeri.method: Relative aperture area equals the square of the assigned diameter ratio. Multiply linear RGB by this area ratio as an exposure illustration.
chironex-fleckeri.evidence: This species constricts its pupils in light and has shown avoidance of dark objects in laboratory observations.
chironex-fleckeri.limits: Camera auto exposure, retinal adaptation and scatter are omitted. No measured constriction time or acuity is fitted; no temporal parameters borrowed from other box jellyfish.
chironex-fleckeri.validation: Digitize species-specific pupil-area time series with uncertainty and compare an independently measured irradiance response.
chironex-fleckeri.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

acanthaster-planci.method: Assign a horizontal field angle to the photograph; average linear RGB within angular cells. The 8° starting value anchors a scenario to reported eye sampling, not a calibrated point-spread function.
acanthaster-planci.evidence: Studies published as A. planci report approximately 8° interommatidial spacing and visually guided orientation toward reef structures.
acanthaster-planci.limits: The A. planci species complex has changed taxonomically. Population transfer, compound-eye geometry, blue sensitivity and slow temporal processing remain unresolved. Pooling is not a detection threshold.
acanthaster-planci.validation: Use locality-matched animals and measured receptive fields; test independent reef and contrast scenes rather than matching this illustration.
acanthaster-planci.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

strongylocentrotus-purpuratus.method: Linear-RGB angular pooling of a rocky habitat. The 10° default is an illustrative scale suggested by a target-detection experiment, not measured receptor spacing.
strongylocentrotus-purpuratus.evidence: Purple urchins oriented toward or away from 10° dark targets; 6.5° targets did not produce significant orientation in that experiment.
strongylocentrotus-purpuratus.limits: Distributed photosensitivity is not a single retinal image. The photograph covers one direction only; body screening, direction of travel and approach versus avoidance are not predicted.
strongylocentrotus-purpuratus.validation: Model body and spine screening, and test different target contrasts and independent animals. Do not convert target diameter directly into grating acuity.
strongylocentrotus-purpuratus.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

schmidtea-mediterranea.method: Collapse each assigned image sector to its mean sRGB-derived luminance. Sector count is a display assumption, not the number of photoreceptors.
schmidtea-mediterranea.evidence: Planarians compare light intensity using cup-shaped eyes; a separate body-mediated UV-A response was demonstrated.
schmidtea-mediterranea.limits: This is an information diagram, not a worm’s image. UV-A is unmeasured, intensity at the animal is unknown, and behavioral choice is not inferred.
schmidtea-mediterranea.validation: Compare calibrated light gradients and ocular/extraocular responses in independent intact animals. No animal intervention is requested.
schmidtea-mediterranea.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

oryctolagus-cuniculus.method: Camera blue and green are displayed as blue and yellow, omitting camera red. The separate monochromatic calculation uses nominal 425/523 nm A1 alpha-band pigment templates; chromophore mixture and ocular filters are omitted.
oryctolagus-cuniculus.evidence: Behavioral spectral modelling supports blue and green cones alongside rods; receptor distribution varies across the retina.
oryctolagus-cuniculus.limits: Camera channels are not rabbit cones. No calibrated color matching, rod interaction, panoramic field or visual-streak reconstruction. Screen hues do not name rabbit sensations.
oryctolagus-cuniculus.validation: Use calibrated reflectance spectra, ocular transmission and brightness-controlled rabbit discrimination data.
oryctolagus-cuniculus.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

lepomis-macrochirus.method: Camera red and green supply a two-channel screen proxy (R, G, G). A separate nominal 536/620 nm pigment calculation uses a hypothetical monochromatic stimulus and an A1 alpha-band template; any A2 contribution is omitted.
lepomis-macrochirus.evidence: Measured green and red cone pigments differ from the action-spectrum peaks obtained under chromatic adaptation; visual resolution also changes with fish size.
lepomis-macrochirus.limits: This is not a calibrated bluegill color transform. Chromophore mixture, ocular filtering, size, water optics and neural adaptation are not fitted; no juvenile UV claim is inferred.
lepomis-macrochirus.validation: Use age- and size-matched spectra and held-out prey tasks. Keep MSP and behavioral action spectra separate.
lepomis-macrochirus.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

oryzias-latipes.method: Keep the habitat photograph as RGB reference. Compare a selected wavelength with the published light-adapted assay endpoints of 740 and 830 nm; no response curve is interpolated.
oryzias-latipes.evidence: LWS-deficient medaka lost part of the long-wave optomotor response when light adapted; dark adaptation changed the result. Seasonal opsin regulation also affects behavior.
oryzias-latipes.limits: The endpoints are not universal visibility cutoffs, confidence bounds, or thermal sensing. Strain, adaptation and stimulus power matter; phone RGB cannot reveal missing spectral channels.
oryzias-latipes.validation: Use trial-level intensity, adaptation and genotype data and independent assays. Do not treat gene count as perceived color dimensionality.
oryzias-latipes.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

homarus-americanus.method: Multiply linear RGB by an assigned gain and report clipped-channel fraction. This is a display experiment; gain is not fitted to the published ERG amplitude.
homarus-americanus.evidence: Adult lobster electroretinograms recorded in constant darkness showed increased responses during subjective night.
homarus-americanus.limits: No new photons or hidden details are recovered. ERG response, detection threshold and perceived brightness are different quantities. No circadian phase is inferred from device time.
homarus-americanus.validation: Fit individual circadian records and noise, then predict independent behavioral thresholds at matched illumination.
homarus-americanus.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

dermochelys-coriacea.method: Average a constant horizontal translation over an assigned exposure interval. Smear angle = speed × integration time; scene width converts this into pixels.
dermochelys-coriacea.evidence: Isolated hatchling retinas did not follow light modulation above 10 Hz in one study. Aquatic eye anatomy does not establish exceptional night vision.
dermochelys-coriacea.limits: The integration interval is an assumption, not 1/10 Hz. No adult temporal response, camera-derived velocity, underwater radiance or gain in photon sensitivity is established. The scene stays still; no flashing stimulus is emitted.
dermochelys-coriacea.validation: Fit an impulse response from raw age-matched ERG data, then compare independent moving-target behavior. Keep hatchling and adult evidence separate.
dermochelys-coriacea.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.
